text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer, and having a clear strategy makes it far less frustrating. The first step is always identifying the bug. Instead of guessing, carefully reproduce the problem and isolate the part of the code where it occurs. A systematic approach is crucial: change one variable or condition at a time, and test after each adjustment. Modern debugging tools are invaluable here—using breakpoints and step-through execution helps you see exactly what the code is doing. Additionally, logging is a simple yet powerful technique. By printing key values to a console or file, you can trace the flow of data and spot where it deviates from your expectations. Remember, patience and methodical thinking solve most bugs faster than random experimentation.
